value.body: A hydrogeologist studies groundwater: where aquifers are, how much water they hold, and how pumping or pollution affects them. Environmental and water consultancies, NGOs working on water security, and infrastructure firms hire them. The work combines field surveys, data analysis and mapping, often for recharge, drinking-water or impact-assessment projects.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc / M.Sc Geology or Applied Geology

items.label: Common tools
items.value: GIS software, field instruments, water-quality test kits

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a water or environmental consultancy, or a water-focused NGO, as a field associate. An M.Sc with hydrogeology specialisation is common for analytical and modelling roles.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior hydrogeologist, project lead, or groundwater modelling specialist.
Water-security programmes and impact assessments drive demand.
Field work in rural and drought-prone areas is common.
